paragraphs: Rav Yitzchak bar Chinena or Chanina.

He was a disciple of R' Huna. In [Ketubot 4b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.4b.3): “Rabbi Yitzchak bar Ch. said: Rav Huna said.” In Ketubot 61b, “R' Yitzchak bar Chanina said: R' Huna said” occurs three times. [Berakhot 52b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.52b.22) has “Rabbi Yosi son of R' Chanina said: Rav Huna said”; this should read R' Yitzchak bar Ch., as in the Rif and Dikdukei Soferim there, note yod. [Nedarim 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.38b.2) has Rav Yitzchak bar Chanania saying “Rav Huna said.” [Sanhedrin 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.38b.2) has Rabbi Yochanan son of R' Chanina; Seder HaDorot suggests that it should perhaps read R' Yitzchak bar Ch., while Dikdukei Soferim there reads R' Chama bar Ch.[^1]

notes.text: The competing heading forms חיננא and חנינא remain Chinena and Chanina. Where Hyman gives only ב״ח/בר״ח, the English retains bar Ch.; בר׳ חנינא is son of R' Chanina, without a default full patronymic honorific. The names Huna and Yitzchak and the work titles Dikdukei Soferim and Seder HaDorot follow the immediate attribution and bibliographic context; they do not establish external identities. The repeated אמר chain remains “said: … said,” not a newly inferred relationship. Hyman’s firm should-read correction in Berakhot differs from Seder HaDorot’s “perhaps” in Sanhedrin; both and every variant remain attributed. The printed colons conventionally give 4b, 61b, 52b and 38b. Note yod remains a letter.

The heading and the Nedarim name retain Hyman’s explicit Rav. William Davidson’s corresponding Hebrew paragraphs explicitly have Rabbi Yitzchak and Rav Huna at Ketubot 4b:3; Rabbi Yosi and Rav Huna at Berakhot 52b:22; Rav Yitzchak and Rav Huna at Nedarim 38b:2; and Rabbi Yochanan at Sanhedrin 38b:2. In Berakhot and Sanhedrin, the checked patronymics say bar Chanina without a full title, so no full title is transferred to the father. The currently numbered Ketubot 61b retrieval did not locate Hyman’s three repeated chains; that label is left as printed, its titles remain R', and no replacement folio is guessed. The quoted Rif, Dikdukei Soferim and Seder HaDorot variant readings have not been independently collated, so their abbreviated titles and conjectural replacements remain R'.
